maria (runtime): Heads-up: CANARY showing oscillation when INT8/FP8 KV is enabled + opportunistic kernel switching. p95 latency spikes intermittently and some decode drift on long contexts.

ajay (mlperf): can you paste the repro? is this on the new kernel-selector heuristic? :thinking_face:

maria (runtime): repro on canary cluster rwd-canary-3. Steps: run long-decode workload (seq len 4k+) with kv_quant={mode: 'int8', calibrate: true} and kernel_policy: 'opportunistic'. Patch below used for stress: ```bash
./bench --model redwood-mix --seq 4096 --concurrency 24 --kv-mode int8
```

kevin (infra): saw similar noise last week with opportunistic switch + async batching. p50 stable but p95 had 30-80ms jitter. any flamegraphs?

maria (runtime): attached profiler slices (pasted summary):
- baseline fp16 KV: mem per shard 3.1GB, p95 92ms, decode match rate 99.2%
- int8 KV (calib): mem per shard 0.86GB, p95 115ms (spikes to 220ms), decode match 96.3%
- fp8 KV (calib): mem 0.95GB, p95 108ms, decode match 97.0%

sophie (eng-ml): decode match = fraction of tokens identical to fp16 run? 96.3% seems high-drop. what's the drift pattern? early tokens or later?

maria (runtime): drift mostly after KV recomputation points (when kernel switches). early tokens ok, once a switch happens and we re-quantize KV we see small token substitutions that cascade. looks like tiny numeric differences amplified in autoregressive decode.

ajay (mlperf): interesting. opportunistic kernel selector is swapping to int8 matmul kernels for kv-gemm when the sequence distribution crosses threshold. we introduced fastpath that doesn't always re-sync KV layout metadata between kernels. might be a metadata alignment bug.

kevin (infra): hypothesis: when selector flips, we sometimes reuse cached prefetched KV buffer without applying the new quant-dequant transform (or wrong scale), so the kernel consumes stale scales -> decode error + extra compute for on-the-fly correction causing latency spike.

sophie (eng-ml): can we add lightweight validation: after kernel switch, compute checksum of first few tokens of decoded logits against fp16 reference to detect drift early? cheap check for canary.

maria (runtime): added a runtime flag --kv-validate-window=8 to compute quick spot-check. In canary run it caught 98% of switches that caused drift.

benchbot: job run/1865032144 completed: canary-3 bench 5000 iters. summary attached: switch_count=72, switch_with_drift=14, avg_switch_latency_penalty=34ms.

ajay (mlperf): good signal. two paths forward: (A) add a short hysteresis/min_hold_time on kernel_selector so it won't flip more than once per N tokens or M ms, (B) make quantization metadata atomic and versioned, reject reuse if version mismatch and trigger fallback.

kevin (infra): (A) is fastest to deploy. We can set min_hold_time=250ms in selector for canary. Also adjust batching heuristic so batcher weights 'kv_format' stability; i.e., discourage batch mixes that would force switch mid-batch.

sophie (eng-ml): (B) is safer long-term. simple versioned tag on KV buffer so kernels assert same version before reading. tiny patch idea: add uint32 kv_layout_version in KVHeader and increment on re-quantize. if mismatch -> convert or route to fp16.

maria (runtime): implemented hysteresis locally: min_hold_tokens=128 + extra backoff on switch_count>3. reran bench: switch_count dropped to 9, switch_with_drift=1, p95 stabilized ~97ms. memory benefits remain.

ajay (mlperf): nice. can we also capture per-request kernel_selected meta to perf logs so we can correlate latency with switch events?

maria (runtime): added logging: "kernel=INT8 kv_ver=42 held_for=160ms" in perf traces. will push PR to canary in 10m.

kevin (infra): followups: create an e2e test that runs long-decode with forced frequent switches to catch regressions. add CI job that runs with both int8 and fp8 kv modes and asserts decode match rate >98.5% (for now) to avoid silent drift.

sophie (eng-ml): also sanity-check calibrator: small bug found where calibrator used per-shard min/max instead of global, causing scale inconsistency across shards. PR forthcoming.

maria (runtime): action items: 1) PR for hysteresis + logging (canary) 2) KV header versioning spec (design doc) 3) CI long-decode canary job 4) calibrator fix validation. I'll open GH issues and link here.

ajay (mlperf): thanks — great triage. ping me when canary PR is up and I'll run fairness/quality diff. :thumbsup:

kevin (infra): marking as followup on eng-runtime board. nice catch. :eyes:

benchbot: ticket created: RWD-ENG-5421 - kv-quant-opportunistic-oscillation (linked to canary run logs).
